note: Reviewed column references the worker makes that no table provides. An entry here is a live gap with a stated consequence, not an accepted pattern — the gate fails on NEW entries, and also on an entry here that has since been created, so this list cannot go stale. Fixing one means deleting its line.

columns.corporate_profiles.kyb_status: services/trust.ts resyncKycKyb reads it to decide whether a kyb_v1 legal_obligation is satisfied. The column exists on no table in this schema, so the SELECT throws into its catch, rows is empty, and the whole KYB reconciliation loop is a no-op. NOT given a column, because that alone would not help: nothing anywhere writes a KYB decision. /trust/kyb/start upserts entity_name, registration_number and registered_country and sets the obligation to in_review; there is no provider callback and no admin approve/reject that would ever set a status. Completing the KYB decision path is feature work and a product question — which store, which values, who writes them — not a rename.
columns.metrics_snapshots.scope: TWO TABLES SHARE ONE NAME, and the worker uses both shapes. Production's metrics_snapshots is a DEAL metrics table — schema_baseline.sql:2994 gives it deal_id, snapshot_date, key_metrics, traction_score, ai_review, created_by plus arr/cac/ltv/… — and routes/pipeline.ts:54 creates exactly that shape at runtime, so it is the one that exists. services/queueWorker.ts instead reads and writes a GENERIC METRIC SERIES (scope, scope_id, metric_name, value, captured_at, extra), which is the sql/historical/infrastructure.sql:38 shape that nothing has built since the migration ledger became the build path. Consequence: the traction_review queue job is dead end to end — its SELECT at queueWorker.ts:85 and its INSERT at :90 both throw 'no such column', so no ai_momentum row is ever written, and the :169 read that would consume one finds nothing. Surfaced only when sql/historical/ stopped being unioned into the harvest; before that the two shapes merged into one 17-column set that satisfied both. NOT renamed here: the two uses want different tables, not different column names, so the fix is to decide whether the series store should exist and under what name — feature work, not a rename. Tracked as its own task alongside the partner_pipeline service_offerings fix that exposed it.
